title: runtime-flag-contracts-and-hot-reload-guidelines-2025
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document defines the contract for runtime configuration flags (a.k.a. feature flags, runtime knobs, and operator flags) and prescribes safe hot-reload procedures for Redwood inference services. The goal is to enable fast operational changes while preserving availability, reproducibility, and model-serving correctness across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Intended audience:
- Service owners and runtime engineers
- Platform engineers who implement config plumbing and validation
- SREs and on-call engineers responsible for change rollout and rollback

Scope:
- Applies to per-service runtime flags, global platform flags, and per-tenant overrides stored in the config-service or injected via environment at process start.
- Covers in-process hot-reload where supported; does not mandate hot-reload for every flag.
- Excludes long-lived data migrations; those follow separate migration playbooks.

Definitions:
- Flag type: runtime, startup, build-time. Runtime flags can be changed without restarting the process if safety checks pass.
- Flag owner: a team responsible for semantic meaning, validation, and telemetry.
- Contract: the schema and compatibility guarantees consumers rely on.

Design principles:
1. Explicit typing and schema: Every flag must declare type, allowed values, default, and a compatibility window.
2. Backwards/forwards safe defaults: New flags default to conservative values that preserve SLOs.
3. Observable changes: All flag updates are emitted as structured events and traced to request/route when possible.
4. Fail-closed for safety-critical flags: If validation or reload fails, the system reverts to the last known-good value and creates an alert.
5. Owner accountability: Flag owners maintain tests and a rollout plan.

Flag schema (required fields):
| field | description | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | dot-delimited flag identifier | service.runtime.enable_prefix_cache |
| type | enum: boolean, integer, float, string, json, enum | boolean |
| default | default value when not present | false |
| allowed_values | comma-separated or range expression | true,false |
| mutability | enum: runtime, startup, build | runtime |
| stability | enum: experimental, stable, deprecated | stable |
| owner | owning team | eng-serving-runtime |
| introduced | semver or YYYY-MM | 2024-09 |
| compatibility_window | date until which callers may rely on current semantics | 2025-09 |
| validation | (optional) regex or JSON Schema reference | ^[a-z0-9_]+$ |

Compatibility guarantees:
- Runtime -> Runtime: changes to a runtime-typed flag will be visible to new request handling paths within 2 seconds and to long-lived sessions according to the KV cache TTL.
- Startup -> Startup: any change to a startup flag requires restart; the config-service must expose a targeted restart API where available.
- Deprecated flags: A flag marked deprecated must include a migration guide and a sunset date.

Hot-reload safety checklist (pre-change):
1. Confirm flag has a runtime mutability and valid schema.
2. Verify automated unit + integration tests covering both true/false or relevant ranges exist and pass in CI.
3. Check SLO impact estimate recorded in the change ticket (expected latency/cost delta).
4. Ensure feature gate can be scoped to < 10% of traffic for canary if behavioral risk exists.
5. Notify on-call and document change window in the deployment calendar.

Change rollout runbook (recommended):
1. Create a change proposal: PR + change ticket referencing flag name, owner, tests, and SLO estimate.
2. Dry-run validation: push to staging config-service and run smoke tests against a canary service.
3. Canary: enable flag for 1% of traffic for 10 minutes. Validate errors, p50/p95 latency, and novel traces.
4. Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 15-minute observation windows. Abort if: error rate > baseline + 3x, p95 latency > baseline + 200ms, or budgeted cost delta exceeded.
5. Full rollout and post-rollout health check: maintain 2 hour watch with automated dashboards and rollback playbook ready.

Rollback procedure (fast path):
- If an immediate failure is detected, toggle the flag back to previous value via the config-service API and trigger a rollback incident.
- If rollback cannot resolve stateful regressions (cache invalidation required), follow the state reconciliation checklist in Appendix A.

Validation and testing matrix:
- Unit tests: owner writes flag parsing/validation tests (required).
- Integration tests: service-level tests that exercise both values and edge cases (required for experimental->stable promotion).
- Chaos test: introduce config-service latency and ensure reload is robust (recommended).
- Static verification: CI job validates flag metadata YAML against the Flag Schema (required).

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- Emit a structured event on every flag change: {flag, old_value, new_value, user, source, timestamp, trace_id}.
- Expose time-series metrics: flag_applied_total{flag,owner,value}, flag_reload_errors_total, flag_reload_latency_ms_p95.
- Instrument request traces to include active flag set hash so that differences can be correlated with errors and model outputs.
- Alerting: create an SLO-aware alert when flag_reload_errors_total > 5 in 5m or when p95 reload latency > 1000ms.

SLOs and operational thresholds:
- Flag change availability: 99.9% of runtime flag updates must be applied within 5 seconds during normal operation.
- Safe rollback time: in 95% of incidents, rollback path must be executed within 10 minutes of detection.
- Observability coverage: 100% of flags in the platform must have change events and metrics enabled.

Security and data considerations:
- Sensitive flags (affecting encryption, key rotation, telemetry PII) must be restricted to admin roles and marked in the schema.
- Config-service writes must be authenticated and audited; retain change logs for 13 months.

Governance and lifecycle:
- Ownership: flag owner is responsible for docs, tests, and the compatibility window.
- Experimental flags: max 3 months in experimental without explicit extension and a migration plan.
- Deprecation: announce 30 days before toggling a stable flag to deprecated; provide migration guidance.

Appendix A — Example flag definition (YAML):

```
# service/runtime-flags.yaml
- name: service.runtime.enable_prefix_cache
  type: boolean
  default: false
  allowed_values: [true, false]
  mutability: runtime
  stability: stable
  owner: eng-serving-runtime
  introduced: 2024-09
  compatibility_window: 2025-09
  validation: null
```

Appendix B — CLI examples (config-service v2):
- Validate metadata: rdx-config validate --file service/runtime-flags.yaml
- Dry apply to staging: rdx-config apply --env=staging --file service/runtime-flags.yaml --dry-run
- Set flag (runtime): rdx-config set service.runtime.enable_prefix_cache true --target=service-prod --actor=asha.patel

Appendix C — State reconciliation checklist (when caches persist old behavior):
1. Invalidate per-worker prefix caches via admin endpoint: POST /internal/admin/invalidate-prefix?worker=all
2. Wait for cache eviction metric to report active_entries=0 per worker.
3. If lingering state exists, coordinate rolling restart of a small worker subset (1% batches).

Ownership and contacts:
- Flag schema and validation library: eng-platform (owner: Marisol Ortega)
- Runtime reload implementation: eng-serving-runtime (owner: Liam Chen)
- On-call escalation: eng-sre (primary: Pager duty rota)

Related reading and references:
- Runtime config best-practices (internal style guide)
- Release and feature rollout pager (oncall-and-incident-response)
- Observability SLI composition playbook

Notes and future work:
- Explore typed dynamic flags with per-request immutable snapshots to eliminate long-lived session drift.
- Evaluate autosuggested rollback thresholds based on historical telemetry.
